When you press your brake pedal, it releases a switch which activates your brake lights. This switch also shuts off cruise control if you have it.
LPT: If tapping your brakes does not turn off your cruise control, your brake lights probably don't work.

This doesn't sound accurate at all. What car does this OP? They are wired separately to the brake pedal. Your cruise control does not rely on your brake lights. They have completely separate controls and wiring harnesses.

I'd wager to say that no car exists anywhere in the world where brake lights and cruise control are on the same circuit and have any causal relationship with each other.

it's not entirely inaccurate. what it was on the 90s GM H-Body cars, was two different switches, both of which rode against the lever of the brake pedal. when depressed, the button on the switch would pop out, and deactivate the cruise/turn on the brake lights. But, in this case, it was two different switches, one for the brake lights, one for the cruise control. Guess which one I needed to replace, and guess which one the auto parts stores never seemed to carry!

90's Toyota's are like this (maybe more). You are making assumptions that you cannot back up. There is also an additional switch on the clutch that will disengage the cruise control as well (if you have a clutch).

This may not be true for newer vehicles but for older ones this is less unusual.

I will offer that a more accurate statement: "If you BREAK LIGHT SWITCH is dead, you're cruise control will also probably not work either".

Depends on how the car is wired. I know that range rovers are wired in the most fucked up way with the cruise control and traction control. I worked on one in the past which would throw a code intermittently. Turns out the traction control read continuity in the tail light assembly, the bulb was fine but had too much corrosion in the terminal.

Some, I'd wager most, cars have two different switches. I can verify that the GM H-Body cars had two, and the auto parts stores never had the cruise control switch in stock, only the brakelight switch.
